title: Sim2Real deployment page · five proposals
brief: Sim2Real opens on Deployments; a deployment shows its 3D and its typed component tree; any node shows the current value of its metrics and gates (the five questions), a nested table like RobotDx's, and before any fit (round 0, 11-15) against now (round 8, 11-17). Each proposal also says where the metric and gate definitions live in the backend.
defaultWhy: Questions leads at 88/100 on the frozen criteria: it answers 'what stops the goal' in one banner, makes the five questions and the parent rule the page's structure, shows every cell before → after, and its backend (sim2real owns the verdict, robot_models stays models-only) is the one that breaks no ruling. Workbench is 2 points behind (86): a fragile lead.
decisionHinge: Familiarity against cause-finding. Move 5 points from fr5 (backend fit) to fr2 (RobotDx conventions) and Workbench wins 88 to 86. The backend axis is separable, so the stronger answer is a splice: Workbench's frame with Questions' banner, question columns and What-changed mode in its Table view, on V4's backend with V2's metrics/ folder if he wants `.metrics` beside `.models`.
invariants: The same fixture: round 0 (as found, 11-15) and round 8 (now, 11-17) scorecards of the pendulum campaign, read-only.
The same 45-node typed tree, the same five questions per node, the same status words and colours (sim2real's tokens).
1440 × 900, dark theme, every variant runnable from file:// and over http, no build step.
Schematic 3D from the station facts, labelled simulated; the CAD render one click away.
boundary: Front-end prototypes over the real fixture. The values a backend would compute are precomputed by fixture/build_fixture.py; each backend is a sketch (BACKEND.md), not implemented in any library.

media.html:
Thesis. a type's metrics sit beside its models, on the same class: IntegratedServo.metrics next to IntegratedServo.m3. Zach's lean ("they should live at the level of the robot models... that's the level at which I describe all of the basic types") taken literally.

metric definition (what, unit, output, which question)robot_models, nested on the familyIntegratedServo.metrics.t3
the five generic questionsrobot_models metrics.FIVE (a base every family's metrics inherits)floor, data, routines, twin, job
gate number (default target)on the Metric; a deployment overrides in sim2real cards/deployments/<dep>.pytarget=at_most(1.5)
current value of a nodesim2real evaluate() → app/data/<dep>/values/<round>.jsonvalues["can11"]["twin"]
fit (does this model explain this log)unchanged: Model.score(log), ModelFamily.select_best(held_out)
health of the physical unitunchanged: RobotDx reads the unit
# robot_models/actuators/servo/integrated_servo_family.py   (beside the models)
class IntegratedServo(ModelFamily, id="integrated_servo"):
    class m3: ...                                        # models, unchanged
    class metrics(Metrics, output="output angle"):       # NEW: model-free, judged at the output
        floor, data, routines, twin, job = FIVE          # generic, inherited
        t3 = Metric("× scatter", question="twin", target=at_most(2.0))     # own to this type
        t7 = Metric("%", question="twin", target=within(5.0))

# robot_models/arms/rigid_body_chain/   (Zach: "a robot arm is just a serial rigid chain"; 1 joint = the pendulum)
class RigidBodyChain(ModelFamily, id="rigid_body_chain"):
    class metrics(Metrics, output="link tip"):
        floor, data, routines, twin, job = FIVE
        tip_stop = Metric("mm", question="job", target=at_most(1.0))       # bam_rack_twin pendulum_goal.Thresholds
        speed_ladder = Metric("of top speed", question="job", target=at_least(0.9))

# sim2real: walk the deployment's typed tree, each node asks its type
values = sim2real.evaluate(deployment, round_dir=".../onedof_2026-11-15/round8")
values.write("app/data/one-dof-test-rack/values/r8.json")        # the page reads only this

Fits:Zach's lean, one place to look per type, .models and .metrics side by side. Strains: the 11-17 ruling "robot_models knows only ModelFamily → Model → Parameter" (a new kind of thing on the family), and robot_models gains a metric runtime it must keep dependency-free.

media.html:
Thesis. Zach's "for now I can just have a folder called metrics where I put this information... I will move it around later". Records, not classes: one module per type id, no family imports it, so moving it later is a git mv. The values are a ledger the table reads row for row.

metric definitionrobot_models/metrics/<type_id>.py, plain MetricSpec recordsMetricSpec("T3", unit="× scatter", question="twin")
the five generic questionsrobot_models/metrics/__init__.py FIVE_QUESTIONS
gate numberon the record (target="<= 2.0"); a deployment overrides in sim2real registry.json
current valueapp/data/<dep>/values.jsonl, one row per node × metric × round
fit / healthunchanged (Model / RobotDx)
# robot_models/metrics/integrated_servo.py
from robot_models.metrics import MetricSpec, FIVE_QUESTIONS
METRICS = FIVE_QUESTIONS.at(output="output angle") + (
    MetricSpec("T3", "current fidelity", unit="× scatter", question="twin", target="<= 2.0", fn="current_over_scatter"),
    MetricSpec("T7", "envelope: top speed", unit="%", question="twin", target="|x| <= 5", fn="top_speed_error"),
)
# robot_models/metrics/__init__.py
def for_type(type_id: str) -> tuple[MetricSpec, ...]: ...      # the registry; nothing else imports these modules

# sim2real writes the ledger; the page's table reads it as is
for node in deployment.tree:
    for spec in metrics.for_type(node.type):
        ledger.append(round=8, node=node.id, metric=spec.id, value=spec.compute(node.runs), status=spec.judge(value))
# {"round": 8, "node": "can11", "type": "pendulum_arm_1dof", "metric": "twin_over_floor", "value": 2.139, "status": "fail"}

Fits:his "folder called metrics" today, and "move it around later" is cheap; the ledger is the same shape as robot_controllers' results.json and W&B rows. Strains: a folder of loose records can drift from the families it describes (no import ties them), and robot_models/metrics/ still puts non-models in robot_models.

media.html:
Thesis. Zach's own sentence, "each RobotPart, just like it has .models, has these performance metrics". The type that joins a datasheet to its models already lives in robotparts (PEP 0004 amendment 2), so the metrics join it there, and the health diagnostics come from the same metrics plus a threshold ("diagnostics build on top of metrics, just adding a threshold").

metric definitionrobotparts, on the part TYPE (never per SKU)robotparts.types.IntegratedServo.metrics
modelsrobot_models, referenced by the typeIntegratedServo.models = robot_models.IntegratedServo
gate numberthe type card's default, a deployment's override
healthdx = Diagnostics.from_metrics(metrics, warn_at=1.25), read live on the unit (RobotDx)unit("moteus-r4.11 · CAN 11").dx
current valuesim2real composes: each tree node points at its part type, type.metrics.evaluate(node.runs)
# robotparts/types/integrated_servo.py
class IntegratedServo(PartType, id="integrated_servo"):
    datasheet = IntegratedServoDatasheet
    models = robot_models.IntegratedServo                    # fit lives on the Model
    metrics = Metrics(FIVE, output="output angle",           # NEW, beside .models
                      own=[T3_current_fidelity, T7_envelope, limiter_share])
    dx = Diagnostics.from_metrics(metrics, warn_at=1.25)     # health = a metric + a threshold, read on the UNIT

part = robotparts.part("jmc-60asm200-ad60g10")               # a SKU: its datasheet values, never its own metrics
unit = robotparts.unit("moteus-r4.11 · CAN 11")              # a physical unit: unit.dx is RobotDx's live health

Fits:his words exactly, and one object answers "what is this part, how do I model it, how is it judged". Strains: robotparts is the catalog (McMaster-style site); judging a composition (a pendulum arm, a cell) is not a part, so the composite types' metrics need a home outside robotparts anyway, and he said robot_parts "shouldn't be specific to each part".

media.html:
Thesis. the verdict lives on a composition (settled, MOC Nov 15), so sim2real owns it. The five questions are generic code, written once; each type contributes only its card: the output it is judged at, its own metrics and its gate numbers. robot_models stays "ModelFamily → Model → Parameter only". The pendulum contract is lifted, not rewritten: bam_rack_twin/pendulum_goal.py becomes the 1-DOF arm's card.

the five questionssim2real/verdicts.py, once for every typefive_questions(node, runs)
a type's own metrics + gate numberssim2real/cards/<type>.py (servo_gates.py is already one)cards/pendulum_arm.py
the parent rulethe card: children=…, gating_children=False (MOC decision 1 default)
current valueCalibrationResult.verdicts() → the site's data/domain/metric_values/<dep>.json (exists today)
fit / healthunchanged: Model.score / RobotDx
# sim2real/cards/pendulum_arm.py   (pendulum_goal.py's Thresholds + cell_gates, moved byte for byte)
CARD = Card(type="rigid_body_chain", joints=1, output="link tip",
            own=[TipStop(at_most(1.0, "mm"), settle=at_most(0.3, "s")),       # Zach's 1 mm
                 SpeedLadder(rungs=(0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 0.8, 0.9, 1.0), goal=0.9),
                 SimPredicts(rel=0.2, abs_deg=0.05)],
            children=("integrated_servo", "rigid_link"), gating_children=False)

# sim2real/verdicts.py
def five_questions(node, runs) -> dict[str, Verdict]:
    """Floor → Data → Routines → Twin → Job at the node's OWN output; a parent passes only with its children."""

result = twin.evaluate()                       # or a scored round
result.verdicts()["can11"]["twin"]             # Verdict(fail, Value(2.14, "× floor"), first=True)

Fits:every settled ruling (fit on the Model, health on the unit, verdict on the composition; robot_models only models); the T-gates already live in cards/servo_gates.py; additive. Strains: a type's metrics are not found "on the type" in robot_models, which is where Zach leaned; two places to look (family for models, card for metrics).

media.html:
Thesis. Zach's "it's almost like robot_metrics". Metrics are model-free functions of logs (robot_msgs trajectories), shared across types (tracking RMS is the same function for a servo and an arm, at a different output), so they get their own small package between robot_msgs and robot_models. A type only names which ones judge it.

metric functionrobot_metrics (depends on robot_msgs only)stop_error_at_tool(traj, fk, stops)
which metrics judge a typeone tuple on the familyRigidBodyChain.judged_by = (...)
gate numbersim2real cards/ targets (as today for T1-T11)
current valueper run → per rung → per node, a ledger per round (results.json), W&B a copy
fit / healthunchanged
# robot_metrics/tracking.py      (new package; robot_msgs only, numpy optional)
@metric(question="job", unit="mm", output="tool")
def stop_error_at_tool(traj: JointTrajectory, fk, stops) -> float: ...

@metric(question="twin", unit="× floor")
def twin_over_floor(real: list[JointTrajectory], sim: list[JointTrajectory], floor: float) -> float: ...

# robot_models/arms/rigid_body_chain/__init__.py
class RigidBodyChain(ModelFamily, id="rigid_body_chain"):
    judged_by = ("floor", "coverage", "oracle_recovery", "twin_over_floor", "stop_error_at_tool", "tracking_rms")

# sim2real: a round is a ledger; the ladder grid is its per-rung rows
ledger = sim2real.score_round(deployment, ".../round8")       # pendulum_score, generalised
ledger.rows(node="can11", rung=0.4)["twin_over_floor"]        # 2.14

Fits:shared functions once (the stock-diagnostics catalog already reduced 89 diagnostics to 30 functions); model-free by construction. Strains: a new package to version and publish (robot-models-lib needed a PyPI name too), and the five questions still need a home (here: sim2real).
